div.div:
Example: N = 8 inputs, the cheater keeps 3 entries (y -> x) for x = 2, 5, 6, so p = 3/8.
For the dropped x: it has thrown away both x and f(x).
For the stored x: it knows f(x) (it is in the table).

For the stored x: it knows f(x) (it is in the table).

div.div:
Average cost per challenge: p * 0 + (1-p) * (1-p)*N/2 = (1-p)^2 * N / 2 hash calls. Always answers correctly.
p = 1: the honest prover (0 calls).
p = 0: pure brute force, about N/2 calls. Less storage means more time (S + T is about N).

text.tspan: Average cost per challenge: p * 0 + (1-p) * (1-p)*N/2 = (1-p)^2 * N / 2 hash calls. Always answers correctly.
p = 0: pure brute force, about N/2 calls. Less storage means more time (S + T is about N).
